name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with +18 partisan lean
Incumbent Jonathan Jackson running for reelection
Huge fundraising gap: Jackson $418K vs Maxwell $63K
model.rationale: The district's +18 Democratic lean, an incumbent seeking reelection, and a lopsided fundraising advantage all point to a comfortable Jackson win, and Polymarket prices him at 96%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting trouble, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 24 points stands.
model.watch: A surprise would require a major external shift in the national environment far beyond what any current evidence shows.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jonathan Jackson, the Democratic incumbent in this Chicago-area district, is seeking another term against Republican Christian Maxwell. The seat sits in territory that leans about 18 points Democratic, and Jackson has out-raised his opponent roughly six to one, with about $47,000 on hand versus Maxwell's $34,000. No outside spending has been reported in the race.

Prediction markets give Jackson roughly a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap, all of which point the same direction. A Jackson victory is the clear expectation.
